analysis.investment_thesis: KSB Limited is a high-quality industrial business with zero debt, 16.4% earnings CAGR, and strong German parent backing — but at 58x P/E with near-zero FCF in FY2025, the market is pricing perfection into a capital-intensive, modest-margin machinery company. I don't pay full price for anything, let alone 44x EV/EBITDA for a pump manufacturer.
key_strengths: Virtually debt-free balance sheet (borrowings just INR 5 Cr vs equity INR 1,679 Cr) — exceptional financial discipline
ROCE of 24.5% and consistent 9-year revenue CAGR of 14% demonstrate a durable, well-run franchise
Strong promoter parent (KSB SE Germany at 69.8%) provides brand credibility, technology access, and governance discipline
key_risks: Extreme valuation — P/E 58x on a ~14-16% grower implies PEG of ~3.5x; I'd need this at half the price to be interested
Capital intensity is concerning — annual capex of INR 94-107 Cr with FY2025 FCF = ~zero despite INR 270 Cr net profit; cash conversion is poor
Cyclical B2B industrial exposure — revenue dipped in FY2020 and growth depends on government infrastructure spending cycles (water, energy, oil & gas)
red_flags: FY2025 free cash flow essentially zero (OCF INR 93 Cr vs capex INR 94 Cr) despite INR 270 Cr reported profit — earnings quality concern
Operating margin only 14.5% — limited pricing power for a specialty machinery company signals moderate, not strong, competitive moat
analysis.detailed_analysis:
KSB Limited is a respectable industrial franchise — a 65-year-old subsidiary of Germany's KSB SE, making pumps and valves for water, energy, chemicals, and mining. The financials tell a story of steady compounding: revenues grew from INR 826 Cr to INR 2,696 Cr over nine years (14% CAGR), net profit from INR 69 Cr to INR 270 Cr (16.4% CAGR), and the balance sheet is essentially pristine with zero meaningful debt and INR 167 Cr cash. ROCE of 24.5% is solid for an industrial company. The business benefits from India's infrastructure buildout in water treatment, power, and industrialization — genuine secular tailwinds. The promoter's 69.8% stake aligns interests well.

However, the valuation demands perfection and then some. At 58x trailing P/E, 42x forward P/E, and 44x EV/EBITDA, the market has already priced in many years of optimistic execution. Worse, FY2025 free cash flow was essentially zero — INR 270 Cr of net profit was entirely absorbed by working capital and capex of INR 94 Cr. This is a capital-hungry business, not the kind of cash machine I love at Berkshire. Operating margins of just 14.5% suggest the pricing power moat is moderate at best — industrial buyers are sophisticated and have alternatives. I'd revisit KSB enthusiastically around 25-30x earnings (~INR 400-500 price range), but at current prices, I'm being asked to pay a wonderful-business premium for a fair-to-good business. That's not my game.
